sent_to_model:
I want to write something for my blog about being single in my twenties. I had ages picked out for becoming a CPA, finding a boyfriend, getting married and having children. Relationships haven't worked out, and I started wondering what was wrong with me. Can you help me reflect on that timetable and explain feeling complete without a partner? I want to reflect on finding security in myself and recognizing God's blessings. I want to encourage other single people to notice their blessings too, and appreciate having a less complicated life. I'd also like a P.S. explaining that I first wrote this at 23 because of a friend, although I don't feel the same about him now.

- Written at 23; later postscript added.
- Family, friends, employment and activities are possible blessings for single readers, not claims about my own circumstances.
- Teenage plan: qualify as CPA at 20, boyfriend at 25, marriage at 30, first child at 32.
- CPA qualification achieved on schedule.
- In my twenties, employed steadily; no apparent personal complications preventing dating.
- A male friend inspired the original reflection; later disappointed in him.
- Tried holding on to relationships and letting them go; several heartbreaks, no lasting partner.
- Affectionate couples sometimes made me feel lonely.
- Reconsidered my plans during a quarterlife crisis.
- Prayed over a long period for a partner; others my age already had relationships.
- Unexpected experiences can be blessings from God.
- Need emotional security within myself.
- Had assumed following expectations would bring a partner.
- Single life feels relatively uncomplicated and less risky.
- Want a partner who encourages growth and makes life more enjoyable.
- Personal effort cannot control another person's choices.
- People and life are imperfect.
- A relationship cannot supply all emotional fulfillment.
- Now feel grateful and complete.
- Insecurity can produce unhealthy dependence between partners.

(About me: accountant and personal blogger. Length: it should come to roughly 400-800 words.)
